ing: pork back fat or fatty pork belly
st: Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil, add the barley, and simmer 35 to 40 minutes until tender. Drain well and cool.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter and prepare a baking dish of hot water to hold it.
Cook the diced pork fat in a skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. Cool for 10 minutes.
Stir the strained blood and the milk together in a large bowl.
Fold in the barley, fat and onion mixture, marjoram, allspice, pepper, and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Pour into the loaf pan and set it in the hot water bath so the water reaches halfway up the sides.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until firm and the center reads 160°F (71°C).
Cool completely in the pan, then chill. Slice thickly.
Fry the slices in a little butter for 2 to 3 minutes per side until crisp, and serve with lingonberry jam.
Rinse the sauerkraut quickly under cold water if you prefer a milder dish, then squeeze it dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the pork in batches for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the sauerkraut, bay leaves, peppercorns, [[1 tsp]] salt, and [[2 cups]] water.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, stirring now and then.
Stir in the barley and [[0.5 cup]] water. Cover and cook another 45 minutes, stirring, until the barley is tender and the pork falls apart at 145°F (63°C) or higher.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes if it is too liquid. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes and a spoonful of sour cream, if you like.
Put the barley and [[3 cups]] water in a pot with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 45 minutes until soft and creamy. Add more water if needed.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Mash the potatoes and stir them into the hot barley.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and beat well until thick and creamy. Add a splash of the potato water if too stiff.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Cook the onion in the bacon fat for 6 minutes until golden.
Spoon the puder into bowls and top with bacon, onion, and a little of the bacon fat. Serve hot.
Boil the whole beets in water for 45 to 55 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Cool, peel, and dice small.
Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes until tender. Cool, peel, and dice small.
Hard-boil the eggs: cover with cold water, bring to a boil, cover off the heat for 10 minutes, then cool in ice water and peel.
Dice 2 of the eggs. Slice the last egg for the garnish.
Toss the beets with the vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Gently fold in the potatoes, herring, pickles, apple, diced eggs, and onion.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] of the sour cream, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper. Taste and adjust.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Top with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sour cream and egg slices before serving.
Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Cool the eggs in cold water for 5 minutes, then peel and slice them.
Spread [[3 tbsp]] softened butter in a thin layer over the rye bread slices.
Lay 3 or 4 sprats side by side on each slice.
Add slices of egg and a few thin rings of red onion.
Top with dill, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Serve right away, or cover loosely and chill up to 1 hour.

ing: 0.25 oz, optional if the broth is not very sticky
st: Rinse the pork well under cold water and put it in a large pot with the onion, 1 carrot, bay leaves, peppercorns, garlic, and [[1 tbsp]] salt.
Cover with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam from the top with a spoon.
Lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer for 3 hours until the meat falls off the bones.
Boil the second carrot in the pot for the last 30 minutes, then slice it into thin rounds.
Lift out the meat. Strain the broth and discard the solids, then boil the broth to reduce it to about [[3 cups]], about 25 minutes.
Pull the meat from the bones and shred it, discarding skin, bones, and gristle.
Sprinkle the gelatin over [[0.25 cup]] cold water for 5 minutes, then stir into the hot broth until dissolved. Taste and add salt.
Put the meat and carrot slices into a loaf pan or deep dish.
Ladle the broth over the top. Chill uncovered at least 6 hours, until firm.
Slice and serve cold with mustard or horseradish and rye bread.

ing: or a mix of toasted barley, rye, oat, and pea flours
st: Rinse the berries and pat them dry. Slice large ones.
Pour the cold kefir into a bowl and whisk in [[3 tbsp]] sugar and the vanilla if using.
Whisk in [[0.75 cup]] kama flour a little at a time to avoid lumps.
Let the mixture stand for 10 minutes so the flour can swell and thicken.
Stir again. If it is too thick, add a splash of kefir. If too thin, add a spoonful of kama.
Spoon into bowls and top with the berries. Serve cold.
Stir the warm water, malt syrup, and molasses together in a large bowl until dissolved.
Add the rye flour, bread flour, yeast, caraway, and [[2 tsp]] salt and mix to a thick, sticky dough. Rye dough stays tacky.
Knead with wet hands for 5 minutes. Cover and let it rise 1 hour 30 minutes until puffy.
Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Wet your hands, shape the dough into a log, and press it into the pan. Smooth the top with a wet spatula.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until the dough is near the top of the pan.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until deep brown and 205°F (96°C) inside.
Turn out onto a rack and cool completely for 2 hours before slicing.
Wrap and rest overnight for the best texture, then slice thin.
If the quark is wet, press it in a cheesecloth or fine strainer over a bowl for 1 hour, then discard the liquid.
Beat the drained quark with [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[4 tbsp]] butter, [[1 tsp]] vanilla, and a pinch of salt until smooth and thick.
Line a plate with parchment. Shape the mixture into 8 short bars about 3 inches long.
Freeze the bars for 40 minutes until very firm.
Melt the chocolate with [[1 tbsp]] butter in a bowl over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Cool 5 minutes.
Dip each cold bar in the chocolate, turning with a fork to coat, then lift and let the extra drip off.
Set the bars on the parchment and chill for 20 minutes to harden.
Store in the fridge and eat within 3 days.
